records.name: Narcotics Anonymous Greater Philadelphia Region
records.summary: The regional service office for Narcotics Anonymous groups in the Philadelphia area. It runs phone lines for people who want to reach someone in recovery right away, and a line that gives meeting information by ZIP code.
records.what_you_do: Call for immediate help or for meeting information, or browse the meeting directory on the website by area, county, virtual meeting, or map. Members can also serve on regional committees such as hospitals and institutions, outreach, public relations, and the phone line.

schedule.text: Meetings run across the region, in person and online, at many different times. The meeting directory and the meeting information line have current times.

locations.label: Mailing address (not a meeting place)
locations.address: 150 Monument Rd, Suite 207-0026, Bala Cynwyd, PA 19004

cost.text: No dues or fees. Meetings run on voluntary member contributions, and literature is sold at cost.

first_step.how: Call 215-NA-WORKS (215-629-6757) for immediate help, or call or text 215-999-4670 for meeting times by ZIP code. You can also pick a meeting from the meeting directory on the website and go to see how it works.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says you do not have to be clean to attend a first meeting, and the Welcome page describes how newcomers are greeted, with a help line and a meeting finder to start.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect an informal meeting of people in recovery from drug addiction, where members take turns sharing or one person speaks at length. Visitors are usually asked to give a first name, and there is no fee to attend. Some meetings are open to people who do not have an addiction and some are closed, so check the listing first.
first_visit_tips: Arrive a few minutes early and stay until the end if you can, and feel free to ask questions.
Choose a meeting marked open if you do not have an addiction yourself.
Be ready to say your first name, which is the usual way to introduce yourself.
Pamphlets are often free at meetings, so you can take one home.

records.notes: The meeting directory listings did not load when read, so no meeting times or open or closed status are recorded. The October 2026 event list includes a newcomer speaker meeting, but it is a one-time event, so it is not in the record. The site's zip-code meeting line is carried in first_step because the contact field holds one phone number.

records.name: Nashirah: The Jewish Chorale of Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: An auditioned community choir that sings the full range of Jewish choral music for audiences in the Philadelphia area. New singers join by audition, and the site shows an audition poster for the 2026 to 2027 season.
records.what_you_do: Audition to join, then sing in rehearsals and perform in concerts. The site lists its concerts by date, but it did not show ticket prices or rehearsal times.

first_step.how: Read the membership terms on the Auditions page, then email manager@nashirah.org to book an audition time. Auditions are by appointment, in person or online.
first_step.basis: Joining requires an audition booked by email and confirmed by the artistic staff, and the site does not show a way to try a rehearsal first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The audition is by appointment, in person or online, and singers are checked on sight-reading, memory for pitch, rhythm, range, and blend. The page does not say how long an audition lasts or what it costs. Arrive at least 15 minutes before your time.
first_visit_tips: Read the membership terms before you book, since applicants are asked to be able to meet them.
Arrive at least 15 minutes before your audition time.
Practice sight-reading and your vocal range, since those are what the staff listen for.

records.notes: Rehearsal days, times, and place are not on any page read, so none are recorded. A web search returned only 2021 to 2022 listings for rehearsals, which are too old to use. The tier 1 claim that the public can attend concerts was not confirmed on any page read, so it was removed from what_you_do. The newest dated item is a June 27 to 30, 2026 Prague festival listed as upcoming with venues still to be announced; last_sign_of_life uses that event month, not a posting date.

records.name: National Alliance of Women Veterans
records.summary: A group that speaks up for women who served in the military. It runs learning, healing, and empowerment work, paying special attention to women who were hurt by military sexual trauma. Women veterans can join, volunteer, or sponsor the work.
records.what_you_do: Women veterans are members by default. You can volunteer, sponsor the work, or register for the 20th Anniversary Tribute on October 24, 2026.

schedule.text: Most of its events are one-time gatherings, such as its anniversary tribute, so check the events page for dates.

locations.label: Mount Airy Church of God in Christ (tribute venue)

cost.text: The group asks for donations and sells merchandise. No attendance fee is listed for its events.

first_step.how: Email info@nawvinc.org or use the contact form to ask about volunteering, sponsoring, or the October 24, 2026 tribute, and register through the link on the group's site.
first_step.basis: Women veterans are members by default and the site invites volunteers and sponsors, but it does not describe a newcomer program or orientation.
first_step.what_to_expect: The October 24, 2026 tribute is a daytime event: breakfast, networking, and registration from 9 to 11 am, a panel and lunch from 11 to 2, and a ceremony at 3:45. Partners named on the page include a veterans home and the Philadelphia VA. The page lists no attendance fee.
first_visit_tips: Arrive at 9 am if you want breakfast and time to register.
The page says registration is open until October 10 but gives no year, so check the registration link for the exact deadline.
Ask the group about parking, transit, and accessibility, since the page does not describe them.

records.notes: The site lists no phone number or mailing address; its contact page offers a form and a 30 minute booking link, and the email comes from the group's events page. Most events on the events page are from 2025. A weekly Women Veterans Speak podcast on Zoom (Fridays, 7 to 9 pm) is listed on that page with no current date, so it is not in the schedule. The site gives three different founding years (1993, 1996, 2000), so none is recorded. Partner Robert Howie Veterans Homes and the Philadelphia VA are named for the tribute and are in leads_only or left out.

records.name: New Beginning Foundation
records.summary: A nonprofit that works to lift up underserved communities through education, literacy, the creative arts and youth development. It hosts fundraisers, outreach events and seminars, and it takes volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer a few hours a week or month, or offer a specific skill. You can also attend a fundraiser or outreach event, or ask about The School of the Heart, a youth development program founded in 2026.

schedule.text: The office is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm. The site mentions an events calendar, but no dated events were shown when checked.

cost.text: No fees for volunteering are listed. The group asks for donations, including a $20 option for its NB Coats for Kids fundraiser.

first_step.how: Email l.denis@nbfoundation-inc.org or call 856-438-0479 during office hours to offer a few hours a month or a skill.
first_step.basis: Volunteering is open to anyone who emails, but the site does not describe what volunteers do and its events calendar showed no dated events, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Your first contact will be by email or phone, since the site does not describe a volunteer orientation or set shifts. The office is open weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm, and the site gives 4544 Greene St as the address with no city or ZIP. Nothing is listed as a fee for volunteering, and the group asks for donations.
first_visit_tips: Call or email during weekday office hours, 9 am to 5 pm.
Ask what volunteer tasks are open and how long a typical shift runs, since the site does not say.
Confirm the address before you go, because the site lists 4544 Greene St with no city or ZIP.

records.notes: Volunteer, event, and program detail is thin. The events calendar showed no dated events, the School of the Heart page gives only a 2026 founding year and no sessions or sign-up steps, and no literacy or tutoring activity is named on the pages read, so the literacy category is carried over from tier 1 and is unverified. Facebook and Instagram were not read, since they are lead-only platforms.

records.name: New Generation Empowerment Ministries
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps young adults ages 18 to 30 meet basic needs and build their well-being through education, programs, and services, across eight areas of wellness.
records.what_you_do: Young adults can ask for basic needs help (such as groceries, hygiene products, or transportation) or housing support through the group's forms. Volunteers can help with events, outreach, mentoring, or behind-the-scenes work. Programs include success coaching, help finding local services, and a workshop series on goals and money.

cost.text: Costs for support are not listed on the website. The group also takes donations.

first_step.how: Email NewGem116@gmail.com to ask how to volunteer, or submit the Basic Needs or Housing Support form on the Get Support page.
first_step.basis: Volunteers can apply by email regardless of background or experience, and support requests use posted forms, but no orientation or first-timer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer roles include event help, outreach, mentoring, and behind-the-scenes work, and time can be as little as about an hour a week. The page does not describe training, orientation, or background checks, so ask by email before you start. After a support request, a team member follows up directly, and housing requests are reviewed as soon as possible.
first_visit_tips: Email NewGem116@gmail.com first, since the site lists no set visit hours.
Ask about training, background checks, and age rules, which the volunteer page does not cover.
For support, ask about eligibility, cost, and the process, which the Get Support page leaves open.

records.notes: The Volunteer and Get Support pages gave the sign-up steps. The site has no dated events or news, so status stays probably_active. The minimum age of 18 comes from the group's definition of its young adult audience, while its volunteer page says anyone can apply, so a reviewer may want to check it. The site lists a mailing address only, with no visit hours.

records.name: New Hope Philly
records.summary: A non-denominational Christian church in Southwest Philadelphia. It offers Sunday worship, separate men's and women's Bible studies, and addiction support for men, including a 12-month discipleship track.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship, join a men's or women's Bible study, or ask about the men's addiction support and discipleship track. The church also lists counseling, Bible school, and GED courses as member supports, with no class schedules published.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am. Men's Bible study on Tuesdays at 7 pm. Women's Bible study on the first and third Saturdays at 11 am.

cost.text: No cost is listed for worship or Bible study. The church invites support through prayer and donations.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am at 5520 Woodland Ave, or call 267-201-2419 or use the contact form to ask about the men's or women's Bible study.
first_step.basis: Worship and Bible studies are listed publicly with times and an address, with a phone number and contact form, but the site gives no visitor guidance and does not explain how to join a study.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 11 am. The website does not describe the service, what to wear, or what visitors do, so it is worth calling ahead. Bible studies meet on Tuesday evenings and on the first and third Saturday mornings, and the site does not explain how to join one.
first_visit_tips: Call 267-201-2419 or use the contact form ahead of time, since the church says it may take 48 to 72 hours to reply.
Confirm the service location before you go, since the church asks for prayer for a building renovation and gives no timeline.
Ask about parking and transit, since the site lists neither.

records.notes: The tier 1 summary said addiction help was for people in general; the what we do page limits addiction support to men, so the summary now says that. The only year on the site is a 2013 footer and there is no dated news, so status stays probably_active. The site asks for prayer for a building renovation with no timeline. The mailing address is P.O. Box 19117, Philadelphia, PA 19143.

records.name: New Jersey Chamber Orchestra
records.summary: A professional nonprofit orchestra based in New Jersey that also plays concerts in Philadelphia, including at the Settlement Music School's Germantown branch. Its mission also mentions educational outreach, with few details on the site.
records.what_you_do: Come to a concert by buying a ticket through the group's site, or give to the orchestra. The site does not describe auditions or other ways to play with the group.

schedule.text: Concerts are listed by date on the website, with no regular weekly schedule shown. Check the concert list before you plan a visit.

locations.label: Concert venue: Settlement Music School Germantown Branch
Office (New Jersey, not a concert venue)

cost.text: Ticket prices are not listed on the pages read. Tickets are sold through the group's ticket link, and the group accepts donations.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for an upcoming concert through the Purchase Tickets link on njchamberorchestra.org.
first_step.basis: Concerts are public and tickets are sold through a clear link, but the site does not describe any way for local players to take part.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a professional orchestra playing a set program, often with guest soloists, some from The Philadelphia Orchestra. The group describes its concerts as intimate and informal, and it can play in smaller venues with about ten musicians. The pages read do not give concert length or ticket prices.
first_visit_tips: Check the concert list on the site for the date and venue before you buy.
Buy tickets through the group's ticket link, since the site does not say whether tickets are sold at the door.
Ask about parking, transit, and accessibility, since the site does not describe them.

records.notes: Verdict left as publish, but a reviewer should decide whether it fits Philadelphia. The group's office is in Collingswood, NJ, and its mission centers on southern New Jersey. The only Philadelphia venue on the site is the Settlement Music School Germantown branch, which hosted its March 14, 2026 concert. If that is not enough to count as serving Philadelphia, the verdict should be out_of_area. The community_band interest is the closest tag for a professional concert orchestra; there is no classical tag.

notes: Seven groups in batch 065, each read from its tier 1 file and its own site. 25 fetches in total (no more than five for any one group) and 1 WebSearch. The single search for Nashirah's rehearsal place returned only 2021 to 2022 listings, which were not used. No page was refused, blocked, or rate limited. The Narcotics Anonymous meeting directory did not load its listings, so no meeting times were recorded. No nearest_septa was recorded because no page named a stop. Tier 1 errors corrected: the New Hope Philly addiction support is for men only; the National Alliance of Women Veterans tribute moved out of the schedule; the Narcotics Anonymous meeting directory link moved out of social media; the New Jersey Chamber Orchestra dated concert moved out of the schedule; the New Beginning Foundation sign-up form claim was not confirmed. Every record is a publish verdict, with the New Jersey Chamber Orchestra flagged for a Philadelphia-fit decision.
